findings.reason: I checked the arithmetic: with user_count=50 and limit=50, floor(50/50)+1 gives 2 pages, so Next becomes enabled and sets offset to min(50,50)=50, and findMembers then fetches an empty page shown as "2/2".

The controller now always applies limit 50 (before, only automatic groups were limited), and members.hbs has no pager, so public pages for non-automatic groups with more than 50 members now show a truncated list with no sign that more exist.

GroupUser keeps user_count through a belongs_to counter_cache, but in Rails 4.1.8 has_many :through delete uses delete_all on the join rows, which skips that counter; Group#remove destroys the rows instead, so this path can leave user_count stale, which feeds the (user_count) label and the pager, and the spec only checks users.count.

Confirmed that addMembers and removeMember have no rejection handlers and that usernames is never reset on the singleton controller (the TODO admits it); this is a real UX gap, but re-adding to another group still needs the user to click Add with the names visible in the input.
Confirmed the automatic-group remove_member spec uses xhr :put while the route is DELETE; this is a minor test-accuracy issue, since controller specs bypass routing.

limit and offset go to SQL unchecked, and Postgres rejects negative values with an error that becomes a 500; unbounded limits were already accepted for automatic groups, so this is input hardening with only an error-path failure.
